# Micro-test: `changelog-entry` step 2 wording

Status: design only. Nothing has been run.

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 make agents write entries that lead with the reader's outcome, without
breaking the one-line, 100-character rule in step 4?

- Old: `2. Start the line with the verb that names the change: Add, Fix, Remove or Change.`
- New: `2. Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers: "Export reports as CSV", "Stop losing the cursor on save".`

Failure type: output has the wrong shape (verb stub plus an internal part name). The new line is a
recipe, which is the right form for that. The proposal names its own risk: the agent drops the
leading verb and writes a sentence over 100 characters. The test must measure that risk as well as
the benefit.

## Arms

| Arm | System prompt |
|---|---|
| OLD | The full current `SKILL.md`, unchanged |
| NEW | The full current `SKILL.md` with only step 2 replaced |

- The prompt is the whole skill, not step 2 alone, because the guidance lives in that context.
- The existing baseline (7 of 10 skipped the rule on the old line) is not reused as the OLD arm.
  Its model, scenario and scoring may differ, so OLD is re-run in the same batch.
- Open item for the partner: I don't have the baseline records in the repo (`specs/` holds only the
  proposal). Say which rule the 7 runs skipped, and I will confirm the rules below match it.

## Models

Two models, 10 reps per arm per model, so 40 reps in all:

1. `claude-haiku-5-5`. The cheapest model, and most likely to take shortcuts.
2. `claude-sonnet-5-5`. The model this session runs on.

I chose these two because you did not name models. Tell me if the skill runs on others.

## Scenarios

Each rep gets one user message: a merged-PR summary and the request "Write the changelog entry."
Use 2 scenarios, each run 5 times per arm per model, so every cell has 10 reps. Each tempts a known
failure:

- S1, internal-leaning: the diff touches `csv_handler.py`, and the PR title is "Fix handler (#482)".
  It tempts "Fix handler" and a ticket number.
- S2, long-leaning: a bug fix with a long and precise cause and effect (cursor lost on save in
  split view after autosave). It tempts a sentence over 100 characters.

The scenario text is identical across arms. It is quarantined from reps (see Isolation).

## Isolation

Follow `references/micro-tests.md`:

- One fresh rep per call, run from a new empty directory outside every repo, with no tools,
  user settings, instruction files or memory.
- Run one probe rep first. Ask what context it sees (instruction files, memory, tools, other
  sessions, user name). Any unplanned answer means fix the setup before scored reps.
- Keep this file, the proposal and the scenario files out of any rep's reach. A rep that reads one
  is VOID.

## Rules (register and commit before reading any reply)

A reply is the text it returns. The entry is the line it proposes.

Mechanical checks, done by a script:

- LEN: the entry is one line of 100 characters or fewer.
- LINES: the reply holds exactly one entry line, with no second change on it.

Read-by-hand checks, done blind:

- OUTCOME: the line says what a reader can now do or no longer suffers.
- NO-INTERNAL: no file, function, module or ticket name stands in for the behavior.

Verdict for a rep:

- PASS: LEN, LINES, OUTCOME and NO-INTERNAL all hold.
- FAIL: any one of them does not hold.
- VOID: the rep read a quarantined file, the probe showed a leak, or the reply is empty or an API error.

A dropped leading verb is not a failure by itself. "Export reports as CSV" has one. "CSV export
works again" has none and can still pass. It counts only through the four checks. Report the number
of entries with no leading verb separately as a side count.

If a reply shows a reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict and report the
counts under both readings.

## Scoring

- Strip the arm, model, order and file names. Give each reply an opaque ID. Grade from those
  sheets. Unblind only after every sheet has a grade.
- Do the mechanical checks by script, then read every reply by hand. Read every flagged match;
  do not trust counts alone.
- Report per model and per arm: PASS, FAIL and VOID counts, the failing check for each FAIL, and
  the side count of entries with no leading verb.

## Decision

Decide before reading: merge when, on each model, NEW has at least 8 of 10 PASS on both scenarios
combined (at least 8 of 10 per model) and has more PASS than OLD. NEW with a length failure rate
above OLD's holds the merge, whatever its OUTCOME gains. If NEW's reps land in five different
shapes, the wording does not bind. Tighten the form before adding words. The merge itself is yours.

## Spend

- Cap: $0.50 for the whole test. Of the budget, $1.50 remains.
- Each rep is a short prompt and a one-line reply. Estimate the cost per rep from the probe rep
  and write it here before the batch.
- Run in 4 batches (one per model and arm pair). Stop when the running total plus the next
  batch's worst case would pass the cap. Record each batch's cost as it finishes.

## Not covered

- Skill-level pressure scenarios. This test checks wording only.
- Models other than the two named above.
